# v1.1 — Keyless backup engines + robustness

Second minor release. Focus: wider engine coverage without sacrificing the
zero-config baseline, and hardening the Node implementation.

## Added

- **Two keyless backup engines** (verified anonymous access):
  - **AnySearch** — `POST api.anysearch.com/v1/search`, envelope
    `{code:0, data.results[]}`; `ANYSEARCH_API_KEY` optional
  - **Keenable** — keyless `/v1/search/public` (requires the
    `X-Keenable-Title` app-identifier header); ephemeral `cards.keenable.ai`
    result URLs are dropped; `KEENABLE_API_KEY` optional for the keyed path
- **Backup opt-in mechanism**: backups are excluded from the default engine
  set (their anonymous quotas are low). Enable per-run with
  `--engine anysearch,keenable` or per-session with
  `EASY_WEB_SEARCH_ENGINES=anysearch,keenable`.

## Fixed

- `fetch.mjs` (Node): structured `{"ok": false}` failure when both the
  direct fetch and the r.jina.ai reader fallback fail, instead of an
  unhandled crash with no output
- `search.mjs` (Node): follow HTTP redirects in `fetchText` — Bing 302s to
  regional hosts on direct (non-proxied) connections, which previously
  failed the whole engine
- `search.mjs` (Node): expanded HTML entity map (`&ensp;` and friends were
  leaking into Bing snippets)
- `search.mjs` (Node): guarded `new URL()` / `JSON.parse` calls with
  structured per-engine error messages

## Changed

- Engine registry now carries flags (`backup`, `optional_key`); engine
  availability logic unified across the Node and Python implementations
- e2e suite rewritten with Node JSON assertions (no `python3` dependency on
  the test host); 15/15 passing, covering backup opt-in semantics end-to-end

## Compatibility

- CLI interface unchanged; no flags removed or renamed
- Default behavior unchanged (ddg + bing baseline; keyed engines join when
  their env key exists)
- Python >= 3.11 / Node >= 18 requirements unchanged
